images.author: Noah_Loverbear
images.title: Boreal Mountain Resort - panoramio (3).jpg
images.describes: Boreal's base-area slopes with two chairlifts running up the hill, a terrain-park fence line and skiers, on an overcast March day.
images.note: Originally a Panoramio upload (2014-03-04), imported by Panoramio_upload_bot and license-reviewed on Commons; geotagged 39.3362,-120.3500 which is Boreal. Flat gray light and a lift tower intrudes at bottom-right, so crop from the upper two-thirds. Prettier alternative if you want a building rather than terrain: File:Ski lodge in Boreal.jpg (5000x2102, CC BY-SA 3.0, Brocken Inaglory) - sunny, already 2.4:1, but it is the lodge, not the slopes.

No usable image found. Wikimedia Commons has no category for Soda Springs Mountain Resort and no file depicting it; the Wikipedia article carries only trail-rating icons and an unrelated 1945 Sno-Cat photo. A Commons geosearch within 2.5 km of the resort (39.3225,-120.3826) returned only railroad, snow-lab and Sugar Bowl photos. Openverse/Flickr under commercial-friendly CC turned up just one on-topic frame: 'DSHS3368_Aerial of snow covered Soda Springs ski resort and Van Norden Dam' (Donner Summit Historical Society, Public Domain Mark 1.0, https://www.flickr.com/photos/188645737@N03/54653571628) - rejected because it is a scanned print with a white border and a large 'Donner Summit Historical Society' watermark burned in, only ~800px, a mid-century aerial whose subject is really the Norden/Van Norden basin, and PDM is a no-known-copyright assertion by a third party rather than a license grant. Everything else current is resort marketing or all-rights-reserved.

images.author: Charliewitkey
images.title: Donner Ski Ranch.jpg
images.describes: Wide winter view across Donner Ski Ranch's runs and the snowy Donner Pass ridgeline, shot from the top of Mount Judah Express at neighbouring Sugar Bowl.
images.note: Already 16:9, so it crops to 300x140 with almost no loss - the lowest resolution of the set but still ~4x the display size. The vantage point is on Sugar Bowl's side of the pass looking at Donner Ski Ranch. A higher-resolution alternative is File:Above Donner Pass.jpg (3648x1566, CC BY-SA 2.0, respiritu) - a gorgeous 2.33:1 panorama shot from Donner Ski Ranch, but it shows Donner Lake rather than the ski area itself.

images.author: Fastily
images.title: Sugar Bowl Ski Resort 8 2012-12-20.jpg
images.describes: Groomed snow at a Sugar Bowl summit lift station under deep blue sky, looking out over miles of white Sierra ridges toward Donner Pass.
images.note: Dual-licensed on Commons as GFDL plus CC BY-SA 3.0/2.5/2.0/1.0 - credit the CC BY-SA 3.0 arm. Author renders on Commons as a styled 'FASTILY'; the account is User:Fastily. Geotagged 39.3012,-120.3228 (Sugar Bowl). The lift terminal occupies the top-left corner; a centre-right crop gives a clean ridgeline panorama.

images.author: John M
images.title: Palisades Tahoe ski area.jpg
images.describes: Sweeping summit panorama over the whole Palisades Tahoe bowl in mid-winter, lift lines and runs threading the basin with Washeshu Peak on the right.
images.note: The best-shaped image of the set - a true 3.2:1 panorama that crops straight into a wide banner. Sourced from Flickr (jsmjr) and passed Commons' FlickreviewR license check on 2024-12-06. Taken 2007, so it predates the resort's rename from Squaw Valley; the terrain is unchanged.

images.author: Leijurv
images.title: Northstar California East Ridge 2019.jpg
images.describes: Freshly groomed run on Northstar's East Ridge lined with snow-loaded pines, opening onto the north shore of Lake Tahoe under a blue sky.
images.note: Shot from near the summit of Mt. Pluto, 2019-02-18; geotagged 39.2412,-120.1389. The strongest-looking picture in the set. Crop the middle band to keep the trees and the lake and drop the empty foreground snow.

images.author: ElijahBizcor (credited on Commons as tahoesignatureproperties.com)
images.title: Skiing in Tahoe.jpg
images.describes: Tahoe Donner's downhill slope on a bluebird day, chairlift and lift shack in silhouette against fresh snow with the sun flaring over the ridge.
images.note: The generic filename is the one caveat: the file says only 'a Tahoe ski mountain'. It is geotagged 39.354183,-120.259103, which is inside Tahoe Donner Downhill Ski Resort, and Commons editors filed it under Category:Tahoe Donner Downhill Ski Resort - it is the ONLY file in that category. Commons renders the author as the bare URL http://tahoesignatureproperties.com/ linked to User:ElijahBizcor; credit whichever form you prefer, but name one of them. Slight sun flare and a lens artefact in the upper-left sky.

images.author: Patrick Nouhailler's…
images.title: Mount Rose Ski Tahoe - panoramio.jpg
images.describes: The Mt Rose front side in full sun - cut runs fanning down a forested peak, a chairlift crossing the frame, and the base lodge with its 'MT ROSE SKI TAHOE' sign at right.
images.note: Panoramio import (2013-04-06), license-reviewed on Commons, geotagged 39.3290,-119.8850 which is the Mt Rose base. The photographer's name genuinely carries that trailing ellipsis - it is the Panoramio display name and is reproduced verbatim in the Commons license template, so print it as-is. Crop left-of-centre if you want the mountain without the lodge signage.

images.license: Public domain (work of the U.S. federal government, PD-USGov-USDA-FS)
images.author: USDA Forest Service, Pacific Southwest Region - photo by Paul Wade
images.title: HeavenlySkiResortLakeTahoe-LakeTahoeBasinMU-PRW-03 (52707087461).jpg
images.describes: Looking out from Heavenly's upper slopes across the full width of a deep-blue Lake Tahoe, snow-covered peaks ringing the far shore.
images.note: The cleanest licensing of the whole set - a US Forest Service work, public domain, no attribution legally required (crediting Paul Wade / USDA Forest Service is still the courteous thing to print). Taken 2023-02-17 for the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit. Crop the upper half; the lower third is featureless groomed snow.

images.author: Roman Fuchs
images.title: Kirkwood Mountain Resort.jpg
images.describes: Skiers spread across a sunlit Kirkwood run with the resort's signature jagged volcanic cliff band rising behind.
images.note: Dual-licensed GFDL plus CC BY-SA 3.0 - credit the CC BY-SA 3.0 arm. Lowest resolution after Donner Ski Ranch but ample for a 300x140 card. If you would rather have no people in frame, File:Backside, Kirkwood, California, 2009.jpg (3072x2304, CC BY 2.0, glenngould) is a dramatic empty shot of the Kirkwood backside peak.

images.author: LittleT889
images.title: Sierra-at-Tahoe 2.jpg
images.describes: Sierra-at-Tahoe's base area on a clear March day - the 'SIERRA at Tahoe Mountain Resort' entrance sign and the Aspen building in the foreground, with the ski hill rising behind.
images.note: The weakest fit for the brief, but it is one of only two Sierra-at-Tahoe files on Commons (the other is an anonymous caution sign) and nothing better exists under a usable license anywhere I searched. It leans base-area/signage rather than open terrain, and the slope behind still shows the thinned, fire-scarred forest left by the 2021 Caldor Fire. Taken 2025-03-08, geotagged 38.8007,-120.0804. Crop the upper-left toward the hill to play down the buildings.

notes: 10 of 11 resorts found; only Soda Springs came up empty. Every image is from Wikimedia Commons and every license was read off the file's own wikitext license template, not inferred - the licenses are CC BY-SA 3.0 (Boreal, Donner Ski Ranch, Sugar Bowl, Mt Rose, Kirkwood), CC BY-SA 2.0 (Palisades), CC BY-SA 4.0 (Northstar, Tahoe Donner), CC BY 4.0 (Sierra-at-Tahoe) and US federal public domain (Heavenly). All ten direct upload.wikimedia.org URLs were fetched and confirmed to return image/jpeg. Every image was also viewed at thumbnail size to check it is not a logo, trail map, portrait or close-up. Sugar Bowl and Kirkwood are additionally offered under GFDL; use the CC BY-SA arm. Attribution requirements: CC BY-SA obliges you to name the author, link the license, and license any adaptation (a crop counts) under the same terms - a caption like 'Photo: Noah_Loverbear, CC BY-SA 3.0' plus a link to the license deed satisfies this. Heavenly is public domain and needs no credit at all. Aspect ratios vary a lot for a 300x140 (2.14:1) slot: Palisades (3.2:1) and Donner Ski Ranch (16:9) crop for free, while the 4:3 shots need a horizontal band chosen deliberately - per-image crop hints are in each note. For Soda Springs, either leave a placeholder or have someone on the trip shoot a photo and release it; the resort's own marketing images are not usable. Searched: Wikimedia Commons full-text, category listings, and geosearch by coordinates; English Wikipedia article image lists; and Openverse filtered to CC BY / CC BY-SA / CC0 / PDM (which aggregates Flickr). No image from a resort website, stock site, news outlet or social media is included.
